fields.meta_title: Suggestion Form Builder: Every Idea Gets a Reply | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a suggestion form that sends each idea to the person who decides on it and emails the sender the outcome. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Suggestion Form That Gets Every Idea an Answer
fields.hero_description: Get a suggestion form that routes each idea to a reviewer and saves every entry in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens to an Idea After Someone Sends It
fields.features_subheading: A slip in a locked box waits until someone opens the box. Each part below moves an idea toward a decision the sender hears about.
fields.feature_1:
Categories that pick the reviewer

The sender picks a category, and the entry goes straight to the person who owns it: tooling to maintenance, menu requests to the kitchen. No one sorts a pile of slips by hand.
fields.feature_2:
A decision date on every idea

You set how many days a reviewer has to decide, and the app sends a reminder before that date passes. A suggestion still open after its date shows as overdue on the review board.
fields.feature_3:
An outcome email the sender reads

When the reviewer marks an idea approved or declined, the app emails the sender with the reviewer's reason. A declined suggestion still gets an explanation instead of silence.
fields.feature_4:
Photos that show the problem

A sender can attach a photo of the leaking valve or the blocked aisle straight from a phone. The reviewer sees what the sender saw, and the file stays attached to the idea.
fields.feature_5:
Every suggestion in a database you own

Entries save to a database you own, with no response caps. Filter a full year of entries by category or by outcome, and count how many of them reached approval this quarter.
fields.feature_6:
One question per screen on a phone

For people who work away from a desk, ask Emergent to build the form as a conversational flow with one question per screen. A suggestion then fits into a short break.

fields.usecase_heading: Suggestion Forms for Four Kinds of Ideas
fields.tab_content_1:
Who decides on a tooling idea, and by when

Kestrel Valve Works sorts every suggestion by category, and Tooling goes to maintenance lead Torvald Ekberg with a decision due in 10 days. Machinist Ines Valdivia suggests a magnetic tray for lathe 4 to catch dropped inserts and attaches a photo. Torvald gets her idea in one email, with the photo and the due date.
fields.tab_content_2:
All 31 voters hear the answer at once

Fieldstone Coffee prints a QR code on its receipts that opens a suggestion form listing open requests first. A customer who wants oat milk cold foam finds it listed and casts the 31st vote instead of starting a new entry. When owner Mika Takahashi puts it on the menu, one email reaches all 31 voters.
fields.tab_content_3:
A card's fifth title request is its last that month

Quarry Hill Library lets each card holder ask it to buy up to 5 titles a month, in print, ebook or audiobook, and the form closes for that card after the fifth. Kofi Asante sends his third request, the audiobook of The Salt Road Letters. Collection librarian Ruth Pellegrini approves it, and Kofi gets an email that it is on order.
fields.tab_content_4:
A tenth of an $8,400 saving, paid as an award

Bellwood Freight pays a tenth of first-year savings as an award and sends suggestions worth over $5,000 a year to its operations director. Dock supervisor Leticia Szabo suggests motion sensors for the dock lights, an estimated $8,400 a year. Once the director approves, the form records an $840 award in her name.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Suggestion Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to set up a suggestion form that gives every idea an owner and a reply by a set date.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide who reads each kind of idea
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the problem before the fix
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the categories people will suggest in, such as safety or tooling, and name one reviewer for each. Give each category one person, not a committee: every suggestion then has someone who answers for it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what is wrong today before asking for the idea, then where it happens, with an optional photo. A clear problem lets the reviewer judge the suggestion even when the proposed fix is not the right one.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose a deadline, such as 10 days from the day an entry arrives, and decide whether a reviewer can ask the sender for more detail before ruling. Print the deadline on the form so senders know when to expect an answer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a plain-English description that covers who reviews each category and what each sender hears back. Emergent builds the form and its review queue, with a database behind them, from that description.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add rules for the bigger ideas
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for each extra rule in a sentence, such as sending suggestions above a savings estimate to a director, or letting people vote on a request that keeps coming back. Change any rule later by prompting Emergent again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one idea in each category from a phone. Check that it reaches the right reviewer, that the reminder goes out before the deadline, and that the outcome email reads well to someone outside the team.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put the link where ideas start
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the link or a QR code where people notice problems: the break room, the intranet home page, or the counter. Add a question asking where the sender found the form. The answers show which spot brings in ideas.

faq_plan.a: A suggestion form is a short form people use to propose a change at work or in a service they use. It asks for the problem they see, the change they suggest, and who is suggesting it. Online, the same form can route every entry to its reviewer and keep a record of the outcome.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a suggestion form?
faq_plan.a: Decide which kinds of idea you will take and who reviews each kind, then write the questions: the problem, the idea, where it happens, and a name if the sender wants credit. Describe all of that to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, and Emergent builds a working form with its review queue. Change any question later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What should a suggestion form template include?
faq_plan.a: Include the problem as the sender sees it, the suggested change, where it happens, an optional photo, and a name field the sender can leave blank. Add a category list if different people review different kinds of ideas. A suggestion form PDF can carry the same questions for a paper box, but someone then has to type every slip into a list.

faq_plan.q: How do I get staff to use an employee suggestion form?
faq_plan.a: Answer every idea, including the ones you decline, and give a reason. Put the link where staff already go for routine forms, such as next to the weekly employee availability form. With the sender's permission, name approved ideas and their authors in team meetings.

faq_plan.q: How should I score ideas from an idea submission form?
faq_plan.a: Score each idea on two scales, such as impact and effort from 1 to 5. For a bigger idea, two or three colleagues score it without seeing each other's scores, and you average them. The category's reviewer still decides. Emergent builds the scales into the review queue from your prompt, and the app can remind each scorer before the decision date.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a suggestion form have?
faq_plan.a: Eight or fewer, with only the problem and the idea required. Ask for detail later, in a follow-up from the reviewer, not on the first screen. Start short and grow it: Emergent changes the form whenever you prompt for a new question.

faq_plan.q: Should a suggestion form ask for the sender's department?
faq_plan.a: Yes, ask for the department or location, because it tells the reviewer where the problem is even when the name is left blank. Skip anything you already keep in each person's employee information form, such as job title or start date.

faq_plan.q: What should a suggestion form do when the same idea keeps coming in?
faq_plan.a: Have it merge the copies into one request with a running count. The number then shows how many people want the change. Reply once to everyone who asked when you decide. The entries sit in a database you own, and a count of repeat requests is one filter away.

faq_plan.q: How should I reply when I turn down an idea from a suggestion form?
faq_plan.a: Say it was declined, give the reason in two or three plain sentences, and name what would change the answer, such as a lower cost or a different site. Write the reply for the sender, not as a copy of the review notes, and invite a revised version. The app can email it to the sender as soon as the reviewer marks the idea declined.

faq_plan.q: Should ideas from a suggestion form count in performance reviews?
faq_plan.a: No, not by default. Keeping suggestion forms apart from reviews lets people send a rough idea without it being judged as performance. To recognize good ideas, keep a list of approved ones and let managers mention them in the employee evaluation form at review time.

Add a category list if different people review different kinds of ideas.' = 6, and categories are the page's core mechanism (feature_1, howto_step_1_des 'List the categories people will suggest in', tab 1). howto_step_7_des then adds a seventh: 'Add a question asking where the sender found the form.' faq 7 adds 'Yes, ask for the department or location'. A reader following the page builds 6-7 questions against its own 'five or fewer'.
findings.fix: Make one count true across the page: either faq 6 says 'Six or seven at most, with only the problem and the idea required' (and still fits faq 3 plus step 7), or trim faq 3 (fold 'where it happens' into the department/location question) and turn step 7's where-found question into a link parameter or QR-code source instead of a question, so the total is five.

findings.quote: Give each category one person, not a committee: every suggestion then has someone who answers for it.
findings.issue: faq 5 contradicts it on the number of reviewers per idea: 'have two or three reviewers score it before they see each other's scores. Average the results'. The how-to says one reviewer, not a committee; the FAQ sets up a scoring panel of two or three. feature_1 ('the entry goes straight to the person who owns it') and tab 1 also say one reviewer.
